title: Meet your Reading List backend
summary: Build a small book-list API with C#, .NET 10 and Oracle. Learn what each part does, then follow a complete project in small steps.
introduction: Imagine a school reading club. One person asks for a book list. Another person finds the list and brings it back. A backend does a similar job for an app. In this course, your C# program receives requests and keeps book records in Oracle.
learningObjectives: Explain the jobs of the browser, API and database
Describe the book-list project you will build
Find the downloadable project and learning path

rows: Shows buttons, a form and the book list.
A small HTML and JavaScript page
Checks a request and sends a useful reply.
Keeps the book records after the program stops.
blocks.caption: The parts of our Reading List app

blocks.text: **C#** is the language we write. **.NET** supplies tools and a runtime, the program that runs our C# code. **ASP.NET Core** is the .NET toolkit for web apps and APIs. **Oracle** stores rows of data. These tools work together, but they do different jobs.

items: You press Refresh list in the browser.
The browser asks GET /api/books for data.
The API asks Oracle for the book rows.
Oracle sends the rows to the API.
The API sends JSON to the browser. The browser draws a list.

blocks.text: An **API** is a set of addresses and rules that programs use to talk. **JSON** is a text format for sharing data. Here is one book as JSON:
The number is the book ID. The title is its name. The value false means the book is still on our to-read list. true means we have read it.

[Download the Reading List project](/downloads/dotnet-oracle-backend.zip). Extract the ZIP before running any command. It contains the API, database scripts, a browser page and a README with all setup steps.

The files are complete. Each lesson explains a small part of them. Keep one copy unchanged so you can compare it with your edits. For earlier skills, follow the [C# .NET and Oracle learning path](/learning-paths/dotnet-oracle-backend).

blocks.title: Where the code runs
blocks.text: This tutorial website stays frontend-only. You run the downloaded C# API and Oracle on your own computer. They cannot run inside this page or on GitHub Pages.
Tell a friend which part keeps the books when you close the browser. Then name the part that checks a new book title before saving it.
